_comment: Pre-registered council ATTENDANCE metrics (road-to-inbox-harvest-2026-08-b Phase 1.4). Registered here rather than in roadmap prose because a roadmap is archived when it closes and a metric outlives it — the sibling budget files (hook-token-budget.json, recycle-threshold-budget.json) already carry the owner / review_by / honest-gap discipline this reuses. The instrument is the quorum_result line appendQuorumEvent writes to agents/runtime/council/events.log (schema v2); nothing here is measured yet, and no threshold is committed before data exists.
privacy: a quorum_result line carries {phase, command, dispatch, verdict, threshold, configured_total, total, present, solo, absent[{member, reason}]} — counts, closed vocabularies, and member ids only. The type has no field able to hold free-form content, so the CLI's own `detail` string (provider error text, which can embed paths and prompt fragments) is dropped at the boundary rather than scrubbed.
phase_split: A pass emits `pre_run` (build_members — who could be constructed) and, on the `run` path, `post_run` (_postRunQuorum — who actually returned a usable response). They disagree whenever a member constructs and then fails mid-flight, so a rate computed over both double-counts. NOT every pre_run line is a pass: `command: estimate` is a spend-free preview, and a `command: run` line is written before the necessity and size-fit gates can abort. That is why `command` exists — every rate below states which values it admits.

attendance_rate.definition: how many of the CONFIGURED members answered: present / configured_total per post_run pass. `total` is the roster that survived construction and `configured_total` the enabled roster before `--single` filtering and before any construction failure — a pass with 3 configured, 2 failing to construct and 1 answering is 1/3, not the 1/1 a `total`-based reading would report.
attendance_rate.instrument: quorum_result lines, phase=post_run, command=run, fields present + configured_total (+ total for the survived-construction split)
attendance_rate.threshold: none committed before data — baseline first, threshold at review date

solo_conclusion_rate.definition: share of post_run passes with `solo: true` — written by the isSoloConcluded predicate in quorum.ts, never re-derived from the numbers here, so one change to the rule cannot leave this definition stale. ceil(n/2) makes 1-of-2 a legitimate conclusion; this measures how often that legitimacy is used, not whether it should be. THREE cases carry solo: true and they are not the same finding — a degraded multi-member council (configured_total > 1), a council configured with one member (configured_total = 1, dispatch = full), and a deliberate --single dispatch (dispatch = single). Split on dispatch and configured_total before reading the rate.
solo_conclusion_rate.instrument: quorum_result lines, phase=post_run, command=run, field solo, split by dispatch + configured_total
solo_conclusion_rate.threshold: none committed before data. The quorum-solo-floor blocker pre-registers the three outcomes this rate decides between — a third CLI member, a gate-scoped min_present: 2, or a published null under 5 % — and that choice is made against real data, never ahead of it. It is decided on the degraded case only; a --single pass is the operator asking for one voice, not the council failing to assemble.

absent_reason_distribution.definition: count per reason over absent[] entries — no_binary / no_auth / timeout / quota (AbsentReason) plus the two runtime fallbacks the CLI writes directly, `unavailable` (transport resolved to nothing) and `binary_missing` (a CLI client refused to construct). Distinguishes a council degraded by configuration from one degraded by provider behaviour, which have opposite fixes.
absent_reason_distribution.instrument: quorum_result lines, absent[].reason, split by phase (a pre_run absence is configuration; a post_run absence is mid-flight) and filtered to command != estimate — a preview reaches construction without running anything, and counting its absences inflates the configuration half.
absent_reason_distribution.threshold: none committed before data — the distribution IS the finding at review date

honest_null_consequence: If the log accumulates and the solo-conclusion rate sits near zero, that is the published answer to the quorum-solo-floor blocker and 1.5 is cancelled against it — not quietly dropped. If attendance data never accumulates at all (nobody runs a metered council pass in the window), that is reported as an unmeasured metric at the review date, never as a passing one.
honest_gaps: `lens` and `invocation` are empty on every pre_run line — neither is known at member-construction time — so any per-lens breakdown is post_run-only.

`command: debate` carries the pre_run half ONLY. There is no _postRunQuorum on the debate path, and defining `usable response` for a multi-round debate is a separate question this registration does not answer. So debate contributes to absent_reason_distribution and to nothing else: attendance_rate and solo_conclusion_rate cover the `run` path, and a reader must not read them as covering every metered pass.

A pre_run line proves construction happened, never that a pass followed — the necessity and size-fit gates can abort afterwards and nothing on the line records it. Any count over pre_run lines is an upper bound.
